content.text: Single continuous cinematic camera move, no cuts. Stylised painterly 3D illustration with the graphic language of a hand-painted game world - bold silhouettes, simplified sculpted forms, soft painterly surfaces without fine photoreal texture detail, and light modelled in clear shapes rather than flat even illumination. Never photorealistic and never live-action, but equally never comic or cartoon. Deep violet and midnight-blue base, structures and light in royal and electric violet. Warm orange only for lamplight, backlight and rim light, never as a colour of the network. This violet-and-orange palette is present in every frame; the image never desaturates into grey or neutral blue. Soft bloom, volumetric haze, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, calm slightly surreal atmosphere. No text, letters, logos, icons or symbols of any kind ever appear anywhere. The dragonfly flies forward through the office, which is already completely threaded with glowing violet network light on every desk, wall, floor and ceiling. That network is already there from the first frame, stays fully lit for the whole shot and never fades, dims or goes dark. She is a precision-engineered machine of dark chrome and anodised violet with large faceted eyes and two pairs of long transparent wings veined with glowing violet nodes - elegant, constructed, never cute or cartoonish. Her wings beat hard and fast in powerful soft-blurred strokes and her luminous violet trail streams continuously behind her. The people are simplified graphic figures, sculpted in broad flat shapes and rim light, with no fine clothing detail, no hair detail and no facial features at all, and they move naturally the whole time: hands typing, a head turning, someone gesturing while speaking, another nodding. As she passes one seated person, that person lifts a hand and waves it quickly through the air beside their head, a small casual reflex, the way someone brushes away a passing fly without even looking up - relaxed and unbothered, never angry, never violent, never a hard strike. She tilts calmly aside and slips past the moving hand without panic, never startled and never knocked off course, and flies on. Just ahead of her, on a desk, lies a neat stack of printed sheets of paper. The sheets are completely blank, carrying no writing, no letters and no readable marks of any kind. She slows, drops toward the stack and settles onto the top sheet, her legs folding under her and her wings coming to rest. The violet light in the room reaches the desk around her and glows along the edges of the stack. Nothing is built or added: the room, the desks, the papers and the people were already there, and only the light is new. The camera follows the dragonfly, which leads the shot and stays visible throughout. The camera never pulls back and never loses the dragonfly. The shot ends with the dragonfly clearly in frame, seen from behind and slightly above, standing still on the stack of blank papers, her wings folded, the glowing violet office around her.
